subtitle: 穿书者也要交材料
sentences: The first time I met Gu Huaichuan was in a duty room off the Ministry of Punishments' east corridor, barely large enough for a single desk.
He was younger than I'd expected, somewhere in his twenties, with an honest-looking face and cuffs washed almost white. Three neat stacks of case files occupied his desk, alongside a chipped teacup.
I poked my head around the door. “Official Gu?”
He didn't look up.
“Petitions go to the west wing. Prison visits, the front courtyard. If you're in the wrong line, go back out and queue again.”
“No, we submitted our petition a few days ago.”
Only then did he raise his eyes. He looked at me, then at Wen Li, and something about his expression shifted.
“Miss Wen. Miss Jiang.”
“You know who I am?” I asked, startled.
“Every three-year-old in the city has heard about the girl who took another bride's place in the wedding sedan.”
I decided I didn't like him.

Wen Li set a receipt bearing an official acknowledgment stamp on the desk. “Official Gu, last time you said we could submit original shipping records to compare against the private accounts. The Jiang family has brought a transcript and impressions of the seals on some old boat tickets.”
Gu Huaichuan took it and gave it a quick glance.
“Where are the originals?”
“Still at home,” I cut in. “Mother's afraid that if we take them out, we'll never get them back.”
“A reasonable concern,” he said.
I blinked.
Who knew the man was capable of saying something human?

“But a transcript alone doesn't establish that the seals or signatures are genuine. If you want these entered as evidence, the person holding the originals must give a statement, and the documents must be examined in person by the authorities. Whether we retain them is a separate question. You can't hand me a sheet of paper and expect me to rewrite the case file.”
“So what are we supposed to do today?”
“Start by separating what you know from what you think you know.”

He pulled several sheets from a stack. The first was headed “Jiang Trading House: Dongping Wharf Vessel Numbers.” The second listed “Government Granary Entry Dates.” The third was a blank witness-information form.
“Did you copy these yourselves?”
I nodded.
“Who copied them?”
“Uncle Qin.”
“Who is Uncle Qin?”
“Our household steward.”
“Full name, address, and what he did at the time.”
“Qin... Well, Uncle Qin's surname is Qin.”
Gu put down his brush and looked at me.
I looked right back.
Wen Li finally lost the battle and turned away to laugh.
“I'll ask him when I get home,” I said through gritted teeth. “Will that do?”
“It will. Come back when you've found out.”
“Official Gu, does everyone who comes in here get this kind of interrogation?”
“Not everyone.”
“Then why am I—”
“Most people know their own steward's name.”
That shut me up for a good while.
Wen Li's shoulders shook with laughter. I glared at her until she forced her face into something resembling composure. “Official Gu, what about the private ledger? What have you found?”

“The Jiang Trading House appears in it. That doesn't prove the Jiang family received or transferred the grain recorded by the government granary. Equally, a departure date on a boat ticket doesn't tell us where the grain ultimately went.”
He lifted one corner of a case file, then closed it again.

“The North River government granary submitted a supplementary receipt register that year. It records eight thousand shi entering storage on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. The copy is attached to the old case, but we don't have the original granary register here. We'll need to request it and check the receiving signatures.”
“Did you see any names on the supplementary register?” Wen Li asked.
“Only the character Yan. The seal beside it is incomplete.”
“Yan Mancang,” I blurted out.
Gu looked up. “Do you know this man?”

“No,” I admitted. “Mother only mentioned him yesterday. He used to work at the North River granary. We heard he might have found work in the southern part of the city, and we're trying to locate him.”
Gu pushed the blank form toward me. “Write down what you know. Don't leave out the word might.”
I picked up the brush and suddenly remembered the job applications I'd filled out after graduating from university, back in my own world.
Education. Address. Emergency contact.
Apparently, getting transported into a novel hadn't saved me from paperwork.
I bent over the page and managed a few characters before Gu said, “Miss Jiang, your handwriting...”
“Is terrible?”
“Not exactly.”
I was just starting to relax when he added, “It looks rather like you've only just learned to hold a brush.”
Without a word, I slid the paper over to Wen Li.
She took it as though nothing were amiss, filled in the details the ministry needed, and didn't ask why I could barely manage a writing brush.
I stole a glance at her and found myself thinking of the drugged tea from the first chapter of this disaster.
She was being almost too considerate toward me now.
We didn't head straight for the southern district when we left the ministry.
Wen Li stood by the gate for a moment, then asked, “Did you sleep well last night?”
“Why?”
“You keep looking at the crossroads.”
“Someone's following us.”
“I saw them too.”
With that, she bought two skewers of candied hawthorn from a street vendor. She pressed one into my hand and kept the other for herself.
“Take the main street.”
“That's what you said yesterday.”
“If it works, it's worth repeating.”

The streets were bustling. The smell of roasted chestnuts drifted from the corner, and someone was singing inside a teahouse. We looped around two blocks, made sure the two men were still behind us, and only then turned into the Jiang family's hauling agency.
Uncle Qin was checking the shipping tags for a convoy. At the sight of us, his face lit up—then immediately grew wary.
“Miss, Madam gave strict orders. Today you're allowed to ask questions, but you're not to borrow a cart, borrow a single man, or disguise yourself as a vegetable delivery girl!”
I stopped dead.
“I haven't even said anything!”
“Madam said those were exactly the things you'd suggest the moment you opened your mouth.”
Wen Li burst out laughing beside me.
Just what sort of person did Mother think I was?

After questioning the older workers, we learned that Yan Mancang had taken occasional jobs at the Cen family's hauling agency in the southern district. They hired laborers to move grain and guard warehouses, with people coming and going so often that some never even gave their real names.

Uncle Qin wanted to send someone he knew to make discreet inquiries first, but Wen Li said, “If Yan really witnessed what happened in the old case, the marquis's household may be looking for him too. The fewer people who know we're asking, the better.”
I nodded gravely. “Then you and I will go.”
“Absolutely not,” Uncle Qin said at once.
“Why not?”
“Because that's the exact opposite of keeping it quiet.”

In the end, Uncle Qin changed into an old laborer's outfit and accompanied us, along with a veteran worker who knew the Cen agency's manager. To avoid drawing attention, we left the Jiang carriage two streets away.

The Cen hauling agency was shabbier than I'd imagined. Empty burlap sacks lay piled outside, wage rates were posted on the wall, and a dozen workers were queuing for their midday meal. The moment the manager heard Yan Mancang's name, his fingers froze on the abacus.
“No one here by that name.”

Uncle Qin gave him a pleasant smile. “A busy man like you can't be expected to remember everyone. But last twelfth month, an older man surnamed Yan was paid here for guarding a warehouse. He had an old injury to his left hand.”
“People come through here all the time. How should I remember?”
That was what he said, but his eyes flicked toward the back courtyard.
I was about to take a look when Wen Li caught my sleeve and gave it a gentle tug.

Instead of pressing the manager, she turned to a young worker wiping down a table. “Excuse me. Was there a Master Yan here late last year who taught you to tie grain sacks? We only want to ask him about something from the past. If you know where he is, perhaps you could pass on a message.”
The young man didn't look up. “Don't know him.”
Wen Li glanced at the worn strip of cloth around his wrist.
“How did that bandage get so dirty?”
“From work.”
“Don't let grain dust get into the wound. If you can, have it changed at the medicine shop on the corner. It won't cost much.”
She set down two copper coins rather than pressing them into his hand. He looked up at her briefly, then lowered his eyes again.
Once we were outside, I couldn't help complaining. “Do you have to play the saint with everyone you meet? We're here to find someone.”
“I know.”
“Then why give him money?”
“His hand was shaking the whole time,” Wen Li said. “Maybe he was afraid of us. Maybe he was genuinely hurt. I didn't want to force him to talk in front of his manager.”
I said nothing.
We were almost at the street corner when the young worker came running after us.
He gripped his sleeves in both hands, his eyes painfully red.
“Are you from the Wen family?”
Wen Li nodded. “Yes. My father was the official who investigated the North River relief grain that year.”
The young man swallowed hard.
“Master Yan isn't dead.”
My heart gave a jump.
“Who said he was dead?”
“The manager told us to say it. If anyone came asking, we were supposed to say he'd fallen ill, died, and been taken back to his village.”
“Where is he now?” Wen Li asked.
“Someone took him away last night.”
“Who?”
“Two men dressed in gray, in a carriage with a gray canopy. One of them showed a token and said the marquis's household wanted to see Master Yan.”
“Did you get a good look at the token?”
“No,” he admitted honestly. “I only saw a gold border.”
My hopes sank at once.
Half the tokens in the city probably had gold borders. How could that prove they were from the marquis's household?
“Did Master Yan get into the carriage willingly, or was he taken by force?” I asked.
The young man thought for a long time.
“He refused at first. Then the men told him someone was already looking after his grandson and that he shouldn't put the boy through another fright. After that, Master Yan went with them.”
Even I couldn't find anything to laugh about now.
“What's your name?” Wen Li asked softly.
The young man took a step back instead. “Are you going to report this to the authorities?”
“Yes.”
His face drained of color, and he turned to leave.

Wen Li didn't stop him. “You don't have to come forward. We'll start by finding out where the carriage came from and where it went. If we eventually need you to testify, we'll tell you what risks you'd be taking before you decide.”
He stood there for a moment, then placed the crumpled copper coins back in her palm.
“I don't want your money.”
His voice was very quiet.
“Master Yan saved half his flatbread for me every day. He said I was too young to keep carrying sacks on an empty stomach.”
Then he ran off.
As I watched him go, those two copper coins suddenly seemed hot enough to burn.
Wen Li didn't say a word on the way back.

Only when we reached the Jiang residence did she take a crumpled scrap of paper from her sleeve. “Someone slipped this under my door two days ago. It only says, ‘Cen Agency. Yan.’ I didn't know who sent it, so I didn't show you.”
I stopped in my tracks.
“Wen Li.”
“Yes?”
“How many more of these things do you have that you ‘didn't show me’?”
After a pause, she said, “A few.”
“Then what exactly are we doing? Looking for people together—or am I just following you around carrying your bags?”
“Do you want the truth?”
“Obviously.”
“I don't dare tell you everything,” she said. “You're Xie Linzhou's cousin, and the Jiang family is involved in the case. I want to trust you. I'm not there yet.”
It was hard to hear, but at least it was better than another vague promise to ‘do my best.’
I didn't answer immediately.
After a while, I handed her the scrap with Cen's name on it.

“All right. Then these are the rules. If it involves your people, you don't have to tell me their names. But whenever you ask me to do something, you have to tell me who might get hurt and what trouble it could bring. Let me decide for myself whether to help.”
Wen Li looked at me.
“All right.”
“You'll remember this time?”
“I will.”
“Should we put it in writing? Official Gu has plenty of forms lying around.”
At last she laughed.
But when her smile faded, her voice turned serious again. “There's something else. If Master Yan really was taken by the marquis's men, he may know where the missing five thousand shi went.”
“Or someone might have been pretending to be from the marquis's household,” I said. “We need to confirm it first.”
Wen Li looked up at me, unusually surprised.
“You're learning fast.”
“That's what getting scolded by Gu Huaichuan does to a person.”
We had barely stepped through the gate when the doorkeeper hurried up with a reply from the Ministry of Punishments.
Gu Huaichuan wanted us to come back the next day.
At the bottom, with no explanation, was a single sentence: One page was missing from the supplementary grain-receipt register attached to the old North River case.
translations: 我第一次见到顾怀川，是在刑部东廊一间小得只能摆下一张桌子的值房。
他比我想象中年轻，二十多岁的样子，眉眼端正，袖口洗得发白。桌上三摞卷宗分得整整齐齐，旁边压着一只缺了口的茶盏。
我从门口探头：“顾大人？”
他没有抬头。
“递状纸去西边，探监去前院。走错了就出去重排。”
“不是，我们前几日递过状纸了。”
他这才抬眼，先看见我，再看见温梨，表情变得有些微妙。
“温姑娘。姜姑娘。”
我惊讶：“您认得我？”
“替人上花轿的事，城里三岁孩子都听说了。”
我决定不喜欢他。
温梨将一张盖了收讫印记的凭据放在桌上：“顾大人，上回您说，若有与私账相对的原始票据，可以呈验。姜家今日带来了一份抄录及旧船票的印样。”
顾怀川接过去，扫了一眼。
“原件呢？”
“还在家里。”我抢着说，“我娘怕带出去就拿不回来了。”
“怕得有理。”他说。
我一愣。
没想到这人居然也会说人话。
“但只凭抄录，不能认定纸上的印与签押是真的。若要作为案证，须让持有人到堂陈述，原件也要经官府当面验看。收存还是留存另议，不能说你们递来一张纸，我就照着改案卷。”
“那我们今天先做什么？”
“先把你们知道的，和你们猜的，分开说。”
他从桌上取来几张纸，第一张写着“姜记东平码头船号”，第二张写着“官仓入册日期”，第三张则是一份空白的证人情况单。
“这些是你们自己抄的？”
我点头。
“谁抄的？”
“秦叔。”
“秦叔是谁？”
“我家管事。”
“姓名、住处、当年的差事。”
“秦……秦叔姓秦。”
顾怀川搁下笔，看着我。
我也看着他。
温梨终于忍不住，偏过头笑了。
“我回去问。”我咬牙，“这还不行吗？”
“行。问清再来。”
“顾大人，您这儿是不是每个人进来都得挨这么一顿？”
“也不是。”
“那为什么我——”
“别人知道自己家管事叫什么。”
我被噎得半天说不出话。
温梨笑得肩膀直抖。我瞪她，她才努力板起脸：“顾大人，那本私账呢？您查到什么了？”
“私账里有姜记，但不能因此断定姜家收过或转过官仓那笔粮。相反，船票有出航日，也不能直接证明粮最终进了哪里。”
他翻开案卷的一角，又合上。
“当年北河官仓上报过一份收粮副册，记着腊月初九入仓八千石。副册如今附在旧案中，但原仓册不在本部。要核实，需追调原簿，查收粮签押。”
“您看过副册上的人名吗？”温梨问。
“只有一个‘严’字，旁边印模不全。”
“严满仓。”我脱口而出。
顾怀川抬眼：“你认识此人？”
“不认识。”我老老实实回答，“昨天才听我娘说起。他以前在北河看仓。我们知道他可能到城南讨过活，正想找。”
顾怀川把空白纸往我这边推了推：“知道的写上。‘可能’两个字别省。”
我提起笔，忽然想起自己穿书前大学毕业时写过的求职表。
学历、住址、紧急联系人。
穿书以后竟然也没逃过填表。
我低头写了几个字，顾怀川忽然说：“姜姑娘，你这字……”
“倒也不是。”
我正要松气，他补上一句：“有些像刚学握笔。”
我默默把纸转给了温梨。
她很自然地接过来，替我把官府要的几项填齐，并未追问我为何连毛笔都握不稳。
我偷瞄她一眼，突然想起第一章那杯药。
她对我已经客气得过分了。
从刑部出来，我们先没去城南。
温梨在门口站了一会儿，忽然问：“你昨晚睡得好吗？”
“怎么了？”
“你总盯着路口。”
“有人跟着。”
“我也看到了。”
她说完，伸手从小摊上买了两串糖葫芦。一串塞到我手里，另一串自己拿着。
“走正街。”
“你昨天也是这句。”
“有用就多说几次。”
街上热闹得很，糖炒栗子的香气从路口飘过来，茶楼里有人唱小曲。我们绕了两条街，确定那两人仍在后头，才拐进姜家的脚行。
秦叔正在看船队的货牌，见我们进门，先是一喜，随后一脸防备。
“小姐，夫人说了，您今日只许问话，不许借车，不许借人，更不许假扮送菜的！”
我当场愣住。
“我还什么都没说！”
“夫人说您一开口肯定就是这几样。”
温梨在旁边笑出了声。
我娘究竟把我想成什么人了？
问过老伙计，我们知道严满仓年前在城南岑记脚行挂过零工。那里专雇搬粮和守仓的人，换人很勤，有些连真名都不留下。
秦叔原想找熟人先探，温梨却说：“他若真见过旧案，侯府恐怕也会找他。别让太多人知道我们在打听。”
我点头，郑重其事地说：“那就我和你去。”
秦叔立刻说：“不行。”
“为什么？”
“因为这句话跟‘别让太多人知道’正好相反。”
最终是秦叔换了脚夫的旧衣服陪我们走一趟，另外带一位认得岑记掌柜的老伙计。为了不惊动人，姜家马车停在两条街外。
岑记脚行比我想象中破旧。门口堆着空麻袋，墙上贴着工钱价目，屋里十几个伙计正排队领午饭。掌柜一听我们找严满仓，手里的算盘立刻停了。
“没这个人。”
秦叔笑了笑：“掌柜贵人多忘事。去年腊月有人从你这里拿过守仓的工钱，姓严，年纪大，左手有旧伤。”
“我这里来的人多，谁记得。”
他嘴上这样说，眼睛却朝后院瞥了一眼。
我刚想过去看看，被温梨在袖子里轻轻拽住。
她没有逼问掌柜，只对旁边擦桌子的年轻伙计说：“小哥，去年年底是不是有位严师傅教过你扎粮袋？我们想问他一点旧事，若你知道去处，帮忙带句话就好。”
年轻伙计头也不抬：“不认识。”
温梨看了看他手腕上的旧布条。
“布条怎么脏成这样？”
“干活弄的。”
“伤口别沾粮灰。你若方便，到街口药铺换一条，不贵。”
她放下两枚铜钱，没有往他手里塞。对方抬头看她一眼，又迅速低下去。
出了门，我忍不住抱怨：“你是不是见谁都想当大善人？我们是来找人的。”
“我知道。”
“你给他钱干什么？”
“他那只手一直在抖。”温梨说，“兴许怕我们，也兴许真受了伤。我不想逼他当着掌柜的面说话。”
我没吭声。
走到街口，那个年轻伙计竟然追了出来。
他两只手攥着袖口，眼睛红得厉害。
“你们是温家的人？”
温梨点头：“是。我父亲就是当年在北河查赈粮的温大人。”
年轻人吞了口唾沫。
“严师傅没死。”
我心里一跳。
“谁说他死了？”
“掌柜让我们这么说。有人来问，就说他病死回乡。”
“他人呢？”温梨问。
“昨晚被人接走了。”
“谁接的？”
“两个穿灰衣裳的男人，坐灰篷车。一个拿着牌子，说是侯府要见严师傅。”
“你看清那牌子了吗？”
“没有。”年轻伙计很诚实，“只看见上头有个金色的边。”
我一下泄了气。
金边牌子满城都有，只凭这个怎么认侯府？
“严师傅是自己上车的，还是被抓走的？”我问。
年轻人想了很久。
“他先不肯走。那两个人说，他孙子已经有人照看，让他别再让孩子受惊。严师傅听完就走了。”
这下连我都笑不出来。
“你叫什么？”温梨轻声问。
年轻人却后退一步：“你们会去报官吗？”
他脸色发白，转身就想走。
温梨没有拦，只说：“你可以不出面。我们先查车从哪里来、往哪里去。若将来必须请你作证，会先让你知道要承担什么风险。”
年轻人站了一会儿，把手里捏皱的铜钱放回她掌心。
“我不要钱。”
他声音很低。
“严师傅每天把自己的半块饼留给我。他说我年纪小，不能老饿着肚子扛麻袋。”
他说完就跑了。
我望着他的背影，忽然觉得那两枚铜钱烫手。
回程路上，温梨一直没说话。
到了姜府门口，她才从袖子里取出一张皱纸：“这是前天有人塞进我门缝的。上面只写‘岑记，严’。我不知道是谁送的，所以没拿给你看。”
我脚步顿住。
“温梨。”
“你是不是还有很多这种‘没拿给我看’的东西？”
她沉默片刻：“有一些。”
“那我们现在到底算什么？一起找人，还是我跟在你后面替你拎包？”
“你想听真话？”
“废话。”
“我不敢把所有事都告诉你。”她说，“你是谢临舟的表妹，姜家也在案子里。我想信你，但还做不到。”
这话难听，却比再来一句“我尽量”好得多。
我没有立刻回答。
过了会儿，我把那张写着岑记的纸还给她。
“可以。那就按这个规矩来。涉及你的人，你可以不说名字。但凡要我去做事，你得告诉我可能害到谁、会惹上什么麻烦。让我自己决定要不要帮。”
温梨看着我。
“这次记住了？”
“记住了。”
“要不写下来？顾大人那儿正好有现成的纸。”
她终于笑了。
笑过之后，却又正色道：“还有一件事。严师傅若真被侯府带走，或许他知道那五千石去了哪里。”
“也可能只是有人冒充侯府。”我说，“得先证实。”
温梨抬头看我，难得有点惊讶。
“你进步倒快。”
“被顾怀川骂出来的。”
我们刚进门，门房便捧着一封刑部的回帖迎上来。
顾怀川让我们次日再去一趟。
信尾没有解释，只写了一句：北河旧案所附的收粮副册，少了一页。

annotations.explain: the first time + 从句 表示首次发生某事的时间，可直接引出回忆。
annotations.example: The first time I visited, it was raining.

annotations.explain: barely + 形容词强调程度很低；large enough for 表示空间够容纳某物。
annotations.example: The room was barely large enough for two chairs.

annotations.explain: I'd expected = I had expected，过去完成时表示在见面之前已有的预期。
annotations.example: The exam was easier than I'd expected.

annotations.explain: 过去分词 washed 表示被洗后的状态，借衣袖细节刻画人物处境。
annotations.example: His old jacket was faded almost white.

annotations.explain: alongside 表示在……旁边；chipped 是“磕掉一块、有缺口的”，不是计算机芯片。
annotations.example: A chipped mug sat alongside the books.

annotations.phrase: poked my head around the door
annotations.explain: poke one's head around/through 表示把头探出来窥看。
annotations.example: She poked her head around the corner.

annotations.explain: look up 在这里是抬起视线，不是查词典。
annotations.example: He didn't look up from his work.

annotations.explain: go to 表示前往；wing 指建筑的一侧或分区，不是翅膀。
annotations.example: The records office is in the east wing.

annotations.explain: line 在美式英语中可指排队，英式常用 queue。
annotations.example: I realized I was in the wrong line.

annotations.explain: queue 作动词，尤其常见于英式英语；此处强化顾怀川一板一眼的态度。
annotations.example: We had to queue again for tickets.

annotations.explain: ago 以说话的此刻为基点；若以过去某时为基点通常用 before。
annotations.example: I sent the letter a few days ago.

annotations.phrase: Only then did he raise his eyes
annotations.meaning: 直到那时他才抬起眼睛
annotations.explain: Only then 置于句首引发部分倒装：did + 主语 + 动词原形。
annotations.example: Only then did I understand the problem.

annotations.explain: something about ... 表示“……的某种地方”；shift 可描写细微态度转变。
annotations.example: Something about her tone changed.

annotations.explain: 嵌入疑问句 who I am 使用陈述语序，不能写成 who am I。
annotations.example: Do you know who she is?

annotations.explain: hear about 是获知有关某件事的消息；hear of 更偏“听说过其存在”。
annotations.example: Everyone has heard about the accident.

annotations.explain: take someone's place 是替代某人的位置或角色，强调实际替代。
annotations.example: I took my colleague's place at the meeting.

annotations.explain: 叙述者即时、主观的幽默判断；不是经过审慎评价得出的客观事实。
annotations.example: I decided I didn't like his attitude.

annotations.explain: bearing 为现在分词作后置修饰，表示“带有、印着”；acknowledgment 指收到的确认。
annotations.example: She showed a receipt bearing the date.

annotations.explain: compare A against B 强调对照标准核查差异。
annotations.example: Compare these figures against the originals.

annotations.explain: transcript 在此是抄录文本，不是影视字幕或学校成绩单；含义取决于语境。
annotations.example: We submitted a transcript of the interview.

annotations.explain: impression 在此指印章留下的印迹，不是“印象”。
annotations.example: The document carried an impression of the seal.

annotations.explain: give sth a glance = glance at sth，常见动词名词转换表达。
annotations.example: He gave the note a quick glance.

annotations.explain: original 作名词时可指原始文件；与 copy、transcript 对应。
annotations.example: Keep the originals in a safe place.

annotations.explain: cut in 是插嘴、打断；也可用于车辆突然插入车道，语境不同。
annotations.example: “Wait,” she cut in.

annotations.explain: get sth back 表示取回、收回；will never 加强担心的结果。
annotations.example: I hope I can get my deposit back.

annotations.explain: reasonable 指合情合理；concern 是顾虑，不一定是直接的恐惧。
annotations.example: That's a reasonable concern.

annotations.explain: be capable of + 名词或 doing 表示有能力；这里是叙述者带讽刺的吐槽。
annotations.example: He's capable of being very kind.

annotations.explain: alone 放在名词后强调“单靠它本身”，不是孤单。
annotations.example: Evidence alone may not prove motive.

annotations.explain: establish 在证据语境中指确立事实；比 suggest 的证据强度高。
annotations.example: The report doesn't establish that he lied.

annotations.explain: enter sth as evidence 是法律语境搭配；这里不是登录电脑。
annotations.example: The photograph was entered as evidence.

annotations.explain: give a statement 可用于向警方或有关部门说明情况。
annotations.example: The witness agreed to give a statement.

annotations.explain: in person 指亲自在现场；与通过副本或转述核对相对。
annotations.example: The documents must be inspected in person.

annotations.meaning: 另一个需要单独讨论的问题
annotations.explain: That's a separate question 可用来区分相关但尚不能混为一谈的事情。
annotations.example: Whether it's legal is a separate question.

annotations.explain: expect sb to do sth 表示期待某人做事；说话者用反问式否定这种期待。
annotations.example: Don't expect me to solve everything.

annotations.explain: be supposed to do 表示按规则、安排或预期应做某事。
annotations.example: What am I supposed to say?

annotations.phrase: separating what you know from what you think you know
annotations.meaning: 把已知事实和自以为知道的事分开
annotations.explain: separate A from B；what 引导两个名词性从句，体现证据与猜测的区别。
annotations.example: Separate what happened from what you assumed.

annotations.phrase: pulled several sheets from a stack
annotations.meaning: 从一摞文件里抽出几张纸
annotations.explain: pull sth from ... 表示从某处抽取；sheet 可以指一张纸。
annotations.example: She pulled a page from the folder.

annotations.explain: be headed 在这里表示文件以某文字为标题，不是“正在前往”。
annotations.example: The letter was headed “Urgent.”

annotations.explain: compound noun 多个词组合限定 form 的用途；witness 指证人。
annotations.example: Please complete the witness-information form.

annotations.explain: 反身代词 yourselves 在此加强主语，强调文件由本人抄写。
annotations.example: Did you build it yourselves?

annotations.phrase: what he did at the time
annotations.explain: at the time 指当时的时间背景，不是“准时”。
annotations.example: She was studying abroad at the time.

annotations.explain: surname 是姓氏；given name 是名，full name 是全名。
annotations.example: Her surname is Chen.

annotations.explain: put down 可指放下物品，也可指贬低某人；这里是字面义。
annotations.example: He put down his pen.

annotations.explain: right back 强调立即或毫不退缩地回应对方动作。
annotations.example: She stared right back at him.

annotations.explain: 字面为“输掉战斗”；在这里指克制笑意失败，属于幽默比喻。
annotations.example: I lost the battle to stay awake.

annotations.explain: grit one's teeth 指咬紧牙关，常用于忍耐、愤怒或疼痛。
annotations.example: “Fine,” he said through gritted teeth.

annotations.explain: will that do 是询问是否够用或符合要求，语气可带不耐烦。
annotations.example: Will two copies do?

annotations.explain: come back when + 时间从句，是常见指示句式。
annotations.example: Come back when you're ready.

annotations.explain: interrogation 本义为审问；用在琐碎问答上产生夸张喜剧效果。
annotations.example: It felt like an interrogation.

annotations.explain: 省略句，完整可理解为 Not everyone gets that treatment。
annotations.example: “Do you agree?” “Not entirely.”

annotations.explain: own 强调“自己所属的”；steward 依历史语境指府邸管事。
annotations.example: She knew every member of her own staff.

annotations.explain: shut sb up 在这里是“让某人无言以对”，比正式说法 silence sb 口语化。
annotations.example: That answer shut me up.

annotations.explain: a good while 表示相当长的一段时间，不是品质好。
annotations.example: We waited for a good while.

annotations.phrase: forced her face into something resembling composure
annotations.meaning: 勉强摆出一副镇定的样子
annotations.explain: force ... into ... 表示硬让……呈现某种状态；resembling 表示“像……但不完全是”。
annotations.example: He forced his face into a smile.

annotations.explain: glare at 指怒视，强于 look at。
annotations.example: She glared at me across the table.

annotations.explain: prove 证据强度明确；避免由账目出现名字跳到当事人参与。
annotations.example: That doesn't prove he knew about it.

annotations.explain: equally 在论证中引出对称的限制，不只是“平等地”。
annotations.example: Equally, we cannot assume she agreed.

annotations.explain: ultimately 表示经过一系列过程后的最终结果。
annotations.example: No one knew where the money ultimately went.

annotations.explain: lift 可以表示抬起或掀开；这里并没有完全打开卷宗。
annotations.example: He lifted one corner of the blanket.

annotations.explain: submit 指正式提交；supplementary 表示补充/附属，register 在此是登记册。
annotations.example: They submitted a supplementary report.

annotations.phrase: records eight thousand shi entering storage
annotations.explain: record + 名词 + doing 可以表示记录某事件发生；shi 为古代粮食计量单位。
annotations.example: The camera recorded him entering the building.

annotations.explain: be attached to 在文书语境是“附随、附上”，不是感情依恋。
annotations.example: The receipt is attached to the report.

annotations.explain: will need to 表示将需要完成某项程序；request 此处为正式调取。
annotations.example: We'll need to request the original file.

annotations.explain: receiving 修饰 signatures，指收货时的确认签字。
annotations.example: We must check the receiving signatures.

annotations.phrase: The seal beside it is incomplete
annotations.explain: beside 表示在旁边；incomplete 表示残缺，不能等同于伪造。
annotations.example: The seal beside the signature was incomplete.

annotations.explain: blurt out 指没有仔细思考就突然说出来。
annotations.example: I blurted out the answer.

annotations.explain: might have + 过去分词表示对过去情况的推测，不能当作已证实事实。
annotations.example: She might have found work elsewhere.

annotations.explain: try to do 强调努力完成；locate 比 find 更偏具体查找下落。
annotations.example: The officers are trying to locate the witness.

annotations.explain: leave out 指省去、漏掉，和 leave behind（遗留在后）不同。
annotations.example: Don't leave out the date.

annotations.explain: pick up 表示拿起，也可指学会技能；这里是动作描写。
annotations.example: She picked up the pen.

annotations.explain: back in ... 回指以前所在的时间或地点，本章涉及穿书身份。
annotations.example: Back in college, I had a part-time job.

annotations.explain: 常见表格固定栏目，不是字面“紧急的接触”。
annotations.example: Write your emergency contact here.

annotations.meaning: 也没让我逃脱文书表格
annotations.explain: save sb from sth 表示使某人免受某事；过去完成时强调穿书已发生。
annotations.example: Moving away hadn't saved me from bills.

annotations.explain: bend over 表示身体前倾；也可用于俯身检查某物。
annotations.example: He bent over the map.

annotations.explain: manage to do/sth 在这里含费劲完成的意味。
annotations.example: I managed a few lines before my hand cramped.

annotations.explain: 用来温和否定对方的猜测，语气不等同于直接说 no。
annotations.example: “Are you angry?” “Not exactly.”

annotations.explain: was just starting to ... 常表示动作初起，随即遭到转折打断。
annotations.example: I was just starting to enjoy myself.

annotations.explain: rather 在英式语境可作程度副词；look like + 从句或名词表示似乎。
annotations.example: It looks rather like a mistake.

annotations.explain: 常置句首作方式状语，表现尴尬或沉默行动。
annotations.example: Without a word, he left the room.

annotations.explain: slide sth over to sb 表示沿表面滑过去，动作比 hand 更含蓄。
annotations.example: She slid the bill over to me.

annotations.explain: as though 引导假设情形；amiss 表示不对劲，were 带非真实语气。
annotations.example: He acted as though nothing were amiss.

annotations.explain: fill in a form/the details 是填写表格；fill out a form 常可互换。
annotations.example: Please fill in the missing details.

annotations.explain: barely 表示仅仅勉强；manage 可指应付某任务。
annotations.example: I could barely manage the heavy suitcase.

annotations.explain: steal a glance 是固定搭配，不表示真正偷窃。
annotations.example: He stole a glance at the clock.

annotations.explain: find oneself doing 表示意识到自己不知不觉正在做某事。
annotations.example: I found myself smiling.

annotations.explain: almost too + 形容词暗示程度反常，带叙述者的疑虑。
annotations.example: He was almost too polite.

annotations.explain: head for 表示朝某地点去，straight 强调不绕路。
annotations.example: We headed straight for the station.

annotations.phrase: Did you sleep well last night
annotations.explain: sleep well 是常见问候关心句；Wen Li 实际在试探她是否受尾随影响。
annotations.example: Did you sleep well after the trip?

annotations.explain: keep doing 表示反复或持续做某事。
annotations.example: He kept looking at the door.

annotations.explain: 现在进行时表示正在发生的动态；follow 可指正常跟随或秘密尾随。
annotations.example: I think someone's following us.

annotations.explain: with that 常用于叙事衔接，将前一句话连接到紧接的动作。
annotations.example: With that, she closed the door.

annotations.meaning: 把其中一串塞进我手里
annotations.explain: press sth into someone's hand 描写带有主动或坚持意味的递物动作。
annotations.example: He pressed a note into my hand.

annotations.explain: take 可与 road, route, street 搭配表示选择行进路线。
annotations.example: Take the main road to the village.

annotations.explain: be worth doing 用主动 -ing 形式表达“值得做”，不接 to do。
annotations.example: This advice is worth repeating.

annotations.explain: bustling 常形容人来人往的街道、市场。
annotations.example: The market was bustling with shoppers.

annotations.explain: drift 可用于气味、烟、声音等缓慢传来。
annotations.example: Music drifted from the next room.

annotations.explain: loop around 表示绕行一圈，以确认尾随者还在。
annotations.example: We looped around the block.

annotations.explain: make sure + 从句是日常高频表达，可指核实或确保。
annotations.example: Make sure the door is locked.

annotations.explain: turn into 可指拐入某条街/地点；也可指变成某物，依语境区分。
annotations.example: Turn into the side street.

annotations.explain: at the sight of + 名词表示“一看见……”，常引出即时反应。
annotations.example: At the sight of the dog, she smiled.

annotations.explain: light up 形容表情因高兴而变得明亮，也可指灯点亮。
annotations.example: Her face lit up when she saw him.

annotations.explain: grow + 形容词可表示状态逐渐变化；wary of 是警惕某事。
annotations.example: He grew wary of strangers.

annotations.explain: give orders 是下令；strict 修饰其要求严厉。
annotations.example: The manager gave strict orders to stay inside.

annotations.explain: be to do 在命令语境表示应当或不得，not to 表示明确禁止。
annotations.example: You are not to enter this room.

annotations.explain: disguise oneself as + 身份/人物，常见于侦查、喜剧情境。
annotations.example: He disguised himself as a waiter.

annotations.explain: stop dead 是突然完全停止，常因震惊。
annotations.example: She stopped dead in her tracks.

annotations.phrase: the moment you opened your mouth
annotations.explain: the moment 可以引导时间从句，等于 as soon as。
annotations.example: The moment he arrived, the room fell silent.

annotations.explain: burst out + doing 表示突然爆发某动作或情绪，如 laughing/crying。
annotations.example: She burst out laughing.

annotations.explain: what sort of ... 用于质疑或强调分类，这里体现自嘲。
annotations.example: What sort of person says that?

annotations.explain: take a job 表示接受工作；occasional 强调不固定、偶尔。
annotations.example: He took occasional jobs on weekends.

annotations.explain: come and go 是固定搭配，常描述人事频繁更换。
annotations.example: Workers were constantly coming and going.

annotations.phrase: never even gave their real names
annotations.explain: not even 表示“甚至……都不”，加强隐蔽程度。
annotations.example: He didn't even give his name.

annotations.explain: make inquiries 表示询问调查；discreet 指谨慎低调，不是 discrete（分离的）。
annotations.example: She made discreet inquiries about the position.

annotations.explain: the + 比较级, the + 比较级 构成“越……越……”，后半句省略至 the better。
annotations.example: The sooner we leave, the better.

annotations.explain: gravely 可表示严肃地；与 grave（坟墓）的字面义不同。
annotations.example: He nodded gravely at the news.

annotations.explain: 比简单的 no 更坚决的拒绝。
annotations.example: “Can I drive?” “Absolutely not.”

annotations.explain: the exact opposite of sth 强调两件事完全相悖。
annotations.example: That's the exact opposite of my advice.

annotations.explain: keep sth quiet 表示不声张，不一定是物理上的安静。
annotations.example: Let's keep the plan quiet.

annotations.explain: change into clothes 表示换衣；区别于 turn into（变成）。
annotations.example: He changed into his uniform.

annotations.explain: along with 是补充伴随成分，动词通常与核心主语保持一致。
annotations.example: She came along with her brother.

annotations.explain: avoid + doing；draw attention 表示引起注意。
annotations.example: We left early to avoid drawing attention.

annotations.explain: 数量词 + streets away 表示距离，away 作后置距离说明。
annotations.example: The bakery is three streets away.

annotations.explain: 比较级 + than I'd imagined；shabby 强调陈旧失修。
annotations.example: The room was shabbier than I'd imagined.

annotations.explain: queue for sth 表示排队等待物品/服务；也可说 line up for。
annotations.example: People were queuing for lunch.

annotations.explain: the moment 相当于 as soon as；引出瞬时触发事件。
annotations.example: The moment she heard the news, she called me.

annotations.phrase: his fingers froze on the abacus
annotations.explain: freeze 可描写因紧张突然不动；不是字面结冰。
annotations.example: Her hand froze on the doorknob.

annotations.phrase: No one here by that name
annotations.meaning: 这里没有这个名字的人
annotations.explain: by that name 表示以那个名字称呼/登记的人；省略了 there is。
annotations.example: There's no employee here by that name.

annotations.explain: can't be expected to + 动词原形表示没有理由要求对方做到。
annotations.example: You can't be expected to know everything.

annotations.meaning: 曾因看守而在这里领工钱
annotations.explain: be paid for doing sth 表示因为完成工作获得报酬。
annotations.example: She was paid for translating the letter.

annotations.explain: come through 可指经过某处；这里不是渡过难关。
annotations.example: Many travelers come through this town.

annotations.explain: flick toward 描写非常短暂的视线移动，常暗示心虚或警觉，但不能单独证明说谎。
annotations.example: Her eyes flicked toward the door.

annotations.phrase: was about to take a look
annotations.explain: be about to do 表示动作马上发生，常被另一事件打断。
annotations.example: I was about to leave when he called.

annotations.explain: give sth a tug 是名词化动作表达，tug 指短促的拉拽。
annotations.example: He gave the rope a tug.

annotations.meaning: 没有继续逼问掌柜，而是……
annotations.explain: instead of + doing 表示不做A而做B；press 在此表示逼问，不是按按钮。
annotations.example: Instead of arguing, she walked away.

annotations.explain: wipe down 表示把表面擦拭干净。
annotations.example: He was wiping down the counter.

annotations.explain: pass on sth 指转交信息、物品，也可指传递知识。
annotations.example: Could you pass on this message?

annotations.explain: 否定动作与前文对话构成回避姿态。
annotations.example: She didn't look up from her book.

annotations.explain: glance at 只表示短暂看一下，通常不暗示长时间注视。
annotations.example: He glanced at the clock.

annotations.phrase: How did that bandage get so dirty
annotations.explain: get + 形容词表示状态变化；so 加强程度。
annotations.example: How did your hands get so dirty?

annotations.explain: get into 表示进入某处；指粮灰侵入伤口，强调实际风险。
annotations.example: Don't let dirt get into the cut.

annotations.explain: have + 物 + 过去分词表示安排别人处理某物，区别于 have sb do。
annotations.example: I had the lock changed.

annotations.phrase: rather than pressing them into his hand
annotations.explain: rather than + doing 表示选择另一种做法；避免直接施压。
annotations.example: She waited rather than interrupting.

annotations.explain: can't help doing 表示情不自禁，不能用 can't help to do 表达相同意思。
annotations.example: I couldn't help laughing.

annotations.explain: play the + 身份名词 常有故作某种姿态的贬义，视语气而定。
annotations.example: Stop playing the hero.

annotations.explain: the whole time 强调某段时间内持续存在的状态。
annotations.example: He was nervous the whole time.

annotations.explain: genuinely 用于强调真实而非装出来的情况。
annotations.example: She sounded genuinely worried.

annotations.explain: force sb to do sth 表示强迫某人做某事。
annotations.example: Don't force her to answer.

annotations.explain: in front of 可表示位置，也可表示在某人面前、当面。
annotations.example: He didn't want to argue in front of the children.

annotations.explain: come running 表示跑着过来；after us 表示追赶目标。
annotations.example: She came running after the bus.

annotations.explain: grip 表示牢牢抓握，动作体现紧张。
annotations.example: He gripped the edge of the desk.

annotations.phrase: Are you from the Wen family
annotations.explain: be from a family 可表示属于某个家族，不必是来自某个地点。
annotations.example: She's from a well-known family.

annotations.explain: swallow hard 常用于紧张、恐惧或难以开口的描写。
annotations.example: He swallowed hard before speaking.

annotations.explain: 否定句揭露关键线索，但不自动证实人物当前位置。
annotations.example: The witness isn't dead.

annotations.explain: heart gave a jump 是受惊或激动的文学化表达。
annotations.example: My heart gave a jump at the sound.

annotations.explain: be supposed to do 在这里表示被交代应当这样做，不代表说法属实。
annotations.example: We were supposed to keep quiet.

annotations.explain: take sb away 可以指带走，不自动断定是依法押解还是胁迫。
annotations.example: Two men took him away in a car.

annotations.explain: dressed in 描述衣着状态，比 wearing 更突出整体装束。
annotations.example: They were dressed in dark coats.

annotations.explain: token 在此指身份牌/凭牌，不是电子令牌或“象征物”的一般义。
annotations.example: The guard showed his official token.

annotations.explain: get a good look at 表示有机会仔细看清。
annotations.example: I didn't get a good look at his face.

annotations.explain: only 限制证人观察范围，不能把“金边”推断成真正侯府令牌。
annotations.example: I only saw the back of the car.

annotations.explain: one's hopes sink 表示期望受挫；是文学化情绪表达。
annotations.example: My hopes sank when I heard the answer.

annotations.explain: How could ...? 用反问指出现有证据不足。
annotations.example: How could this prove he was there?

annotations.explain: willingly 强调出于本人意愿；与 by force 对立。
annotations.example: She went willingly.

annotations.explain: by force 指使用强制手段；对事实认定需要证人补充说明。
annotations.example: He was taken by force.

annotations.explain: at first 表示最初阶段，通常暗示之后发生变化。
annotations.example: She refused at first but later agreed.

annotations.explain: look after 表示照顾；在威胁话语中可故意含糊是否安全。
annotations.example: Can you look after my dog?

annotations.phrase: put the boy through another fright
annotations.explain: put sb through sth 表示使某人经历困难或不愉快事件；这里隐含威胁。
annotations.example: I won't put you through that again.

annotations.phrase: couldn't find anything to laugh about
annotations.explain: find something to laugh about 指找到可笑之处，否定式表达气氛突然严肃。
annotations.example: There was nothing to laugh about.

annotations.explain: take a step back 字面可指退后，也可比喻重新评估；这里为真实动作。
annotations.example: He took a step back from the door.

annotations.explain: report sth to sb 表示向主管机关报告；authorities 指有关当局。
annotations.example: We reported the theft to the authorities.

annotations.explain: drain of color 是因恐惧、震惊而失去血色的固定描写。
annotations.example: Her face drained of color.

annotations.explain: turn to do 表示转身开始另一动作；不是 turn to sb 求助。
annotations.example: He turned to leave the room.

annotations.explain: come forward 在调查语境是出面提供信息或承认证词。
annotations.example: A witness finally came forward.

annotations.explain: start by doing 表示以某一步骤作为起点；find out 表示查明事实。
annotations.example: Start by finding out the date.

annotations.explain: need sb to do sth；testify 属法律语境，表示提供证词。
annotations.example: They may need her to testify.

annotations.explain: would be taking 在假设未来作证情形下描述可能承担的风险。
annotations.example: Understand what risks you'd be taking.

annotations.explain: before 引导时间从句，强调先知情后决定。
annotations.example: Read it before you decide.

annotations.phrase: placed the crumpled copper coins back
annotations.meaning: 把捏皱的铜钱放了回去
annotations.explain: place sth back 表示放回原位/某人手中；crumpled 描写受攥压的形态。
annotations.example: She placed the key back on the table.

annotations.explain: want + 名词直接表示需求；此处反映年轻工人的动机不是索取报酬。
annotations.example: I don't want your money.

annotations.explain: on an empty stomach 是固定短语，常和 work, drink, travel 搭配。
annotations.example: Don't exercise too hard on an empty stomach.

annotations.phrase: those two copper coins suddenly seemed hot enough to burn
annotations.meaning: 那两枚铜钱忽然像烫手一样
annotations.explain: seem + 形容词；hot enough to burn 夸张地表现愧疚与震动，不是真实高温。
annotations.example: The cup was hot enough to burn my fingers.

annotations.explain: not say a word 强调完全沉默，常用于情绪转换后的过渡。
annotations.example: She didn't say a word on the drive home.

annotations.explain: slip sth under 表示悄悄或顺手塞进某物下面。
annotations.example: Someone slipped a note under the door.

annotations.explain: who sent it 为宾语从句，语序是陈述句语序。
annotations.example: I don't know who sent this email.

annotations.explain: show sb sth / show sth to sb 是常见双宾结构；这里涉及隐瞒信息。
annotations.example: Why didn't you show me the letter?

annotations.explain: stop in one's tracks 指走动中突然停下，常因震惊。
annotations.example: I stopped in my tracks when I heard it.

annotations.phrase: How many more of these things
annotations.meaning: 你还有多少这样的东西？
annotations.explain: How many more 强调在已知数量之外仍有更多。
annotations.example: How many more questions do you have?

annotations.explain: exactly 用于疑问句加强追问，表示要对方明确解释。
annotations.example: What exactly do you mean?

annotations.explain: follow sb around 指到处跟随某人，可能带抱怨意味。
annotations.example: Stop following me around.

annotations.explain: 字面是携带行李，在此比喻自己被当成跑腿角色。
annotations.example: I won't just carry your bags.

annotations.explain: want the truth 用于预告即将说出可能难听但坦诚的内容。
annotations.example: Do you really want the truth?

annotations.meaning: 不敢把所有事都告诉你
annotations.explain: dare (to) do 表示敢于做某事；否定句尤其常见。
annotations.example: I don't dare ask him.

annotations.explain: be involved in 可表示关联/牵涉，不必说明有罪。
annotations.example: Her name was involved in the investigation.

annotations.meaning: 我现在还做不到那一步
annotations.explain: not there yet 表示尚未达到某种程度或心理状态，口语常见。
annotations.example: I want to forgive him, but I'm not there yet.

annotations.explain: hard to hear 可以指听不清，也可以指话语令人难受，此处为后者。
annotations.example: That was hard to hear.

annotations.explain: at least 常用来在负面情况下指出有限的积极面。
annotations.example: At least we know where to begin.

annotations.explain: vague 指缺乏明确内容；promise to do sth 为承诺行动。
annotations.example: I don't want another vague promise.

annotations.explain: immediately 表示马上；否定可写出人物谨慎权衡而非马上同意。
annotations.example: He didn't answer immediately.

annotations.phrase: whenever you ask me to do something
annotations.meaning: 凡是你要我做事的时候
annotations.explain: whenever = every time that，强调任何一次出现该情形。
annotations.example: Call me whenever you need help.

annotations.explain: bring trouble 表示引发问题；could 表示可能性而非确定结果。
annotations.example: We discussed what trouble it could bring.

annotations.explain: for oneself 表示独立做出决定，不由他人代替。
annotations.example: I want to decide for myself.

annotations.explain: will 在此不是纯粹预测，而是要求承诺；this time 对比之前失信。
annotations.example: You'll tell me first this time, right?

annotations.explain: put sth in writing 是正式或半开玩笑要求书面确认的常用表达。
annotations.example: Could you put that in writing?

annotations.explain: lie around 指物品闲置放着，常暗示不缺；与 lie（说谎）不同。
annotations.example: There are spare notebooks lying around.

annotations.explain: fade 可描写光线、颜色、声音，也可描写情绪逐渐消散。
annotations.example: His smile faded when he saw the letter.

annotations.phrase: If Master Yan really was taken
annotations.explain: if 引导条件句，really 强调事件尚未经证实；不能改写为肯定事实。
annotations.example: If the witness really was there, ask him.

annotations.explain: may 是概率性推测；where 引导宾语从句，保持陈述语序。
annotations.example: She may know where they went.

annotations.explain: pretend to be 表示假装某种身份；证据不足时提出替代解释。
annotations.example: He was pretending to be a guard.

annotations.explain: confirm 指核实真假；first 突出判断次序。
annotations.example: We need to confirm the details first.

annotations.explain: unusually 表示与人物惯常反应不同，为角色变化服务。
annotations.example: She looked unusually nervous.

annotations.explain: present continuous 的 you're learning 表示近期学习进步，语气可带打趣。
annotations.example: You're learning fast in this job.

annotations.explain: get + 过去分词可表达遭遇某事，较 be scolded 更口语。
annotations.example: He got scolded for being late.

annotations.explain: had barely done ... when ... 表示刚完成前一动作，后一事件立刻发生。
annotations.example: I had barely sat down when the phone rang.

annotations.explain: hurry up with sth 在此配合上前动作；与催促 Hurry up! 有区别。
annotations.example: She hurried up with the letter.

annotations.explain: want sb to do sth 表示希望或要求某人做某事。
annotations.example: The doctor wants me to come back tomorrow.

annotations.explain: at the bottom 可指页面/信件最下方，也可指物体底部。
annotations.example: The address was printed at the bottom.

annotations.explain: with + 名词短语用作伴随状语，说明附带情况。
annotations.example: The letter arrived with no explanation.

annotations.explain: be missing from 表示某物本该属于某整体却不在其中。
annotations.example: One page is missing from the file.

annotations.phrase: attached to the old North River case
annotations.explain: 过去分词 attached to 作后置修饰；强调文件归属而非内容真伪。
annotations.example: The notes attached to the report were incomplete.

scenes.title: 刑部值房
scenes.alt: 刑部东廊的值房里，顾怀川坐在案前翻看文书，姜明月与温梨带着材料前来。

scenes.title: 填写证人单
scenes.alt: 案几前，姜明月拿毛笔填写证人情况单，温梨递纸，顾怀川公事公办地核对。

scenes.title: 正街糖葫芦
scenes.alt: 人潮熙攘的正街上，温梨递给姜明月一串糖葫芦，远处似有人跟随。

scenes.title: 岑记脚行
scenes.alt: 岑记脚行内堆着麻袋和账册，秦叔与脚行掌柜交涉，姜明月和温梨在旁旁听。

scenes.title: 脚夫低声交代
scenes.alt: 街角处，衣衫破旧的年轻脚夫低声透露线索，姜明月掌心压着铜钱，温梨认真倾听。

scenes.title: 门前线索纸条
scenes.alt: 姜府门前的暮色中，温梨展开皱纸给姜明月看，两人谨慎交换新的线索。

scenes.title: 缺页回帖
scenes.alt: 灯下案前，姜明月与温梨一起阅读刑部回帖，意识到旧案副册缺了一页。
